title: Policy-driven adjudication & smart suppression for usage alerts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
Currently multiple detectors surface noisy anomalies (usage/cost/latency) which create alert storms for SREs and customers. Existing guards are static thresholds or simple suppression windows; they do not account for tenant volatility, cross-metric correlation, or business impact. This yields high false positive rates, alert fatigue, and delayed triage for critical incidents.

Goal:
Build a policy-driven adjudication layer that consumes anomaly candidates from upstream detectors, scores and adjudicates them with tenant-aware impact, and applies smart suppression and routing policies before creating Console alerts/notifications. The system should reduce false positives by 50% for medium-impact alerts while preserving high recall for critical incidents.

High-level design:
- Ingest: anomaly candidates published to Kafka topic telemetry.anomaly_candidates by detectors (batch and streaming detectors).
- Enrichment: realtime enrichment service queries tenant-metadata-service for billing tier, active routes, and SLOs and attaches recent token-exposure and SLA weight. Enrichment is cached in Redis with 2m TTL to keep latency < 150ms.
- Scoring: lightweight rule engine + ML model (logistic regression for initial rollout) computes an impact_score, noisiness_score, and confidence. Rules encode business policies (e.g., exclude scheduled maintenance windows, apply higher weight for enterprise tenants).
- Suppression/adjudication: policy engine applies suppression windows that are adaptive: window length = base_window * volatility_factor where volatility_factor is derived from 30d rolling variance of the metric for the tenant. Policy engine also deduplicates correlated anomalies across metrics (cost vs usage vs latency) using temporal and tenant grouping.
- Routing & actions: alerts with impact_score >= critical_threshold -> immediate PagerDuty + Console banner. impact_score in medium range -> Console alert + Slack digest (hourly), with optional auto-mitigation runbook (e.g., scale up dedicated pool) if customer has dedicated capacity.
- Storage & audit: adjudication decisions and derived signals are written to ClickHouse table console_anomaly_decisions for downstream dashboards and for audit/forensics (retention 90d).

Implementation notes/choices and trade-offs:
- Streaming vs batch: core adjudication runs in Flink (stateful streaming) to keep end-to-end decision latency < 1s for high-severity candidates. A slower batch job will recompute scores for candidates with low confidence for retrospective analysis.
- ML model complexity: start with a logistic regression trained on historical labeled alerts (last 12 months) for explainability. Migration path: gradient boosted tree if precision/recall targets not met.
- Privacy: tenant-level sensitive attributes are only used for scoring within the VPC; anonymized or aggregated attributes stored in ClickHouse. Must coordinate with Security for PII-safe enrichment.
- Operational constraints: must be horizontally scalable; per-tenant state kept in keyed state store (Flink state backend with RocksDB). Cold-start tenants default to conservative policy to avoid missing critical incidents.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to move to In Review):
- Precision: false positive rate for non-critical alerts reduced by >= 50% vs baseline (Oct-Nov 2024 window).
- Recall: critical incidents recall >= 98% (based on labeled dataset).
- Latency: 95th percentile adjudication latency <= 1s for streaming path.
- Auditing: every outgoing alert has an adjudication record persisted with reason code and impact_score.
- Ops: runbook for manual override & suppression exists and tested end-to-end (Playbook link below).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged beta to internal SRE + 3 pilot customer tenants for 2 weeks. Monitor precision/recall and MTTI.
2) Expand to 20% of traffic with automated telemetry gating.
3) Default on for all tenants after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: Console -> Observability -> Anomaly Adjudicator (latency, impact distribution, suppression rate, per-tenant signal). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/observability/anomaly-adjudicator
- Alerting on regressions: automated regressions detector (linked) will open a ticket if suppression rate increases > 2x week-over-week.

Open questions / risks:
- Labeled dataset coverage: our labeled incidents skew towards high-severity; need more medium-impact labels to train for better discrimination. Action: Solutions team to curate 300 medium incidents (owner: PM).
- Cross-tenant correlated incidents (global infra events) may be suppressed incorrectly. Mitigation: global-signal bypass that elevates correlation across >X tenants into critical path.
- Storage cost for high cardinality decisions in ClickHouse. Mitigation: aggregate rollups for long-term retention and keep raw for 90d only.

Next steps (short-term):
- Build Flink prototype + rule-engine baseline (Sprint 2).
- Data labeling sprint with Solutions/Support (due 2025-02-05).
- Security review kickoff for enrichment service (due 2025-01-29).
